Hi Olivia / Ben,

Great to meet earlier today - thanks for the time and for walking us through the Acme integration use cases. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we demoed:
- Streaming responses (token-by-token) with partial structured outputs for UI responsiveness
- Tool/function calling (we demoed a prototype integration for your order enrichment flow)
- Structured outputs (JSON schema validation + reranking hooks)
- How Redwood routes requests between dedicated and burst capacity to preserve latency SLOs

Key differentiators vs hyperscalers you asked about:
- Latency predictability under load (dedicated pools + KV cache can keep 95p token latency consistent)
- Cost levers: batching + prefix caching vs pay-per-token only models
- Tooling: per-route dashboards and rollout controls we can hand to your platform team

Proposed next tests (we recommend running these in parallel):
1) Streaming latency test: run your representative prompt set with simulated concurrent users to check first-token and tail latency vs your target.
2) Tool-calling parity: exercise the order-enrichment function call patterns (see attached acme-test-plan.xlsx) and compare structured output fidelity.
3) Throughput/cost: run a 1-hour sustained batch to measure tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf (high-level feature/cost diff), acme-test-plan.xlsx (test cases + sample payloads).

Next steps / asks from Acme:
- Share a 1-2 hour slice of representative prompt traffic or a synthetic harness (we can accept anonymized payloads).
- Allocate a small test account for us to push a demo config (we can spin up a short-lived Dedicated emulator).
- Preferable window for the live test: next week Tue/Wed (Nov 30 / Dec 1).

I copied Vivek and Rishi to handle technical setup and run the tests - we'll own the execution and report back with results and recommended config changes.

Hi Olivia - great questions, answers below and some suggested test implementations.

1) Nested function outputs: supported. Redwood's function-calling layer can accept and validate JSON schemas with nested objects/arrays. We run a two-step validation: schema conformance + lightweight semantic checks during post-processing.

2) Streaming function responses: we currently support streaming tokens while the model is building the response. For true "function-streaming" (incremental function payloads), we have two recommended patterns:
   - Pattern A (recommended): stream tokens and buffer until a JSON object completes; emit partial JSON fragments to UI with a confidence flag. This preserves token-streaming guarantees and is compatible with SSE / chunked HTTP.
   - Pattern B: use a WebSocket-based multiplexed channel if you need out-of-band signals (e.g., long-running function progress + intermediate structured events).

For React/Next.js we typically recommend SSE or fetch with ReadableStream - easiest to integrate with existing streaming libraries and server components. We'll share a small client snippet in the Drive link.

3) Ballpark pilot estimate: for a 10M token/month pilot over 3 months, assuming a mix of streaming + function calls and modest KV cache hit rates, expect ~$18k- $25k/month on Hosted. Dedicated pricing (reserved pool) would lower unit cost by ~30% but requires a minimum reservation. We can put formal numbers in the SOW once we know traffic distribution.

Suggested immediate test matrix (what Vivek will run with Acme test harness):
- Test A: 200 concurrent users, 1-2 prompt roundtrips per user, measure first-token latency and 95/99p tail.
- Test B: Function-calling parity: 500 calls with nested JSON outputs; assert schema pass rate and downstream parsing error rate.
- Test C: Streaming UX: render partial JSON in UI and measure perceived time-to-first-valid-field.

I've attached redwood-technical-notes.pdf with implementation details and the client streaming snippet.

If that looks good, Marissa / Rishi - we'll need a test account and the anonymized payload by EOD Monday (Nov 30) to start Tuesday.

Thanks,
